built.what:
BUG-065 is fixed. The security audit no longer claims MFA or inactive-user results it does not track, and only members with settings read can run it.

Server (`apps/server/src/modules/security-audit`):
- Every check now carries a `status`: passed, failed or not_tracked. `passed` stays and is true only when the status is passed.
- **MFA check:** it is now not_tracked. It states no percentage, no member count and no recommendation, and it no longer reads the memberships. It used to report a hard-coded `mfaRate = 1` as "100% of team members have MFA enabled" and count it as a pass.
- **Inactive-users check:** it is also not_tracked, because no last sign-in is recorded. It used to hard-code `inactive = 0` and pass. This is a small extension beyond the MFA wording; see open_issues.
- **Score:** a new exported `summarizeAudit` counts only measured checks in score, passed and total. A new `notTracked` field counts the rest, and score is null if nothing was measured.
- **Access:** GET `security/businesses/:businessId/audit` now runs `ModuleScopeGuard` with `@RequireModuleScope('settings', 'read')`. A member without settings read gets 403 before the audit reads anything; the test proves this with a spy on `runAudit`.

Web (`apps/web/src/app/app/settings/security/page.tsx`):
- A not-tracked check shows a 'Not tracked' label and is drawn as neither a pass nor a failure, with no recommendation.
- The summary reads 'N of M checks passed · K not tracked'.
- A 403 shows an alert headed 'No access, ask the owner' (matching the journey J6 wording) with the line 'Ask the business owner for access.' It shows no score, no checks, no toast and no 'Run audit' button.
- Other errors still show a toast.

findings.claim: This was already true before the packet, and it is outside the packet's scope. The audit's config checks (env-secrets, ssl-config, rate-limiting, password-policy) describe the whole deployment's process.env, not the tenant. The new settings:read gate is scoped to a business, so it does not protect this deployment-wide information. Any user who owns a business (every self-signup is an OWNER, D-03) can read the platform's secret-configuration posture. That includes the oracle line 'SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is identical to the public anon key', which would tell an attacker that the anon key in the browser bundle is the privileged key. Values are never shown, only flags. Suggested follow-up: make the platform-config checks SUPER_ADMIN only, or remove them from the tenant audit. Not a reason to block this packet.
findings.failure_path: Reproduced on a real DB (keyflowos_v1_swp_sec_audit_truth_sec, branch head 1d068715a, the packet's own harness with the real AuthMiddleware, AuthGuard, BusinessGuard, ModuleScopeGuard and TenantInterceptor). Setup: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY set to the same value (built from fragments), and AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_API_KEY set to a short value. Actor: user v63r_outsider, who is OWNER of their own business v63r_bizB and has no link to any other tenant. Request: GET /security/businesses/v63r_bizB/audit. Response: 200, and the env-secrets check reads {severity:'critical', status:'failed', description:'Issues: AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_API_KEY appears short/weak; SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY appears short/weak; SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is identical to the public anon key; DATABASE_URL points to localhost'}. Any other tenant's owner gets the same answer, because the check reads process.env and never businessId.

After restoring the head code it passes again.

**Who can run the audit.** I read the guard path: ModuleScopeGuard, resolveRequestBusinessId (path, then body, then query) and memberModuleLevel. The route now needs settings read, and both guards check the business named in the path, which is the one the handler uses. Extra probes I wrote and ran on the real DB:
- **P1:** the owner of business B names A in the path and B in the query, the x-business-id header and a JSON body. Result: 403 'No access to this business' from BusinessGuard, and runAudit never ran.
- **P2:** an ADMIN whose explicit map sets settings to 'none' (D-114). Result: 403 'settings requires read access (you have none)'.
- **P3:** an ADMIN whose permissionScopes is an empty array, which counts as an explicit empty map. Result: 403.
- **P4:** a member with role 'owner' in lowercase, which falls back to the STAFF defaults. Result: 403.

The packet's own cases also cover a STAFF member on the role defaults (403), a STAFF member whose map leaves settings out (403), a STAFF member with settings 'read' (200), ADMIN (200), OWNER (200) and a non-member (403). In every refusal the spy shows runAudit did not run.

- The answer holds only counts and flags: no personal data, no secret values, and no new logging.
- The 403 body is the standard guard message.

**Web page.** The security page uses apiGet's status. On a 403 it clears any earlier result, so nothing from another business stays on screen, and shows the refusal notice without a score, checks or the Run audit button. Its 4/4 tests pass.

findings.claim: apps/web/src/app/app/settings/security/page.tsx treats every 403 as a settings refusal: `if (res.status === 403) { setResult(null); setRefused(true); return; }`. BusinessGuard also answers 403 when it cannot complete its check: 'Unable to verify business access' on any database error, and 'Service unavailable' when Prisma is missing (core/auth/business.guard.ts). In that case an OWNER is told 'No access, ask the owner ... Ask the business owner for access.' and the 'Run audit' button is hidden, so the owner cannot retry without reloading the page. At base the same 403 showed a toast and kept the button. The repo already has a helper for exactly this distinction, isModuleScopeRefusal(res, 'settings') in apps/web/src/lib/module-scope-refusal.ts (review CRR-P195JS-2: 'Any other 403 (BusinessGuard's transient "Unable to verify business access" or "Service unavailable"...) says nothing about it, so a screen must not tell the member they lack the module'). The page does not use it.
findings.failure_path: Server, reproduced on real Postgres with the packet's own harness (real AuthMiddleware, AuthGuard, BusinessGuard and ModuleScopeGuard, the real controller and service). Actor: OWNER v63g_owner. Request: GET /security/businesses/v63g_biz/audit. With no lock it answers 200. A second session runs BEGIN; LOCK TABLE businesses IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE (6 s), and the server pool has statement_timeout 1500 ms. The same OWNER request then answers 403 {"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"Unable to verify business access"} (Postgres 57014, statement timeout, caught by BusinessGuard). After the lock is released the request answers 200 again. Web, reproduced with a vitest probe of the page, apiGet answering {data:null, error:'Unable to verify business access', status:403}: the alert reads 'No access, ask the ownerThe security audit reads this business's settings. Ask the business owner for access.', the Run audit button is absent and no toast fires. 'Service unavailable' renders the same way. Repair: show the notice only when isModuleScopeRefusal(res, 'settings') is true (optionally also BusinessGuard's 'No access to this business'). Any other 403 keeps the toast and the Run audit button. WEB-SAT-03 uses ModuleScopeGuard's refusal text, so it stays green; add a case for the transient 403.

built.what:
Fix commit ef4df3c86 changes three files.

**SEC-W1FPMS-3 (genome money memory, D-128/D-100)**
- UnifiedMemoryRetrievalService now selects the GenomeMemoryEvent row's domain and section. Every genome fragment carries the row's sourceType, eventType, domain and section in metadata.genomeRow (GENOME_ROW_METADATA_KEY in unified-memory.types.ts). These are written after the row's own metadata, so a writer's metadata cannot stand in for them.
- readersOwnPromptMemory now projects genome records too (recordModulesOf → genomeModulesOf). It is the shared rule of buildMemoryContext, the pipeline's chatMemoryFragments and the /ai flow chat perception block (so also the staff bridge).
  - A money memory event needs revenue read. "Money" is the rule the genome REST routes already apply (isMoneyMemoryEvent): FINANCE_GENOME or a finance-filed row, CROSS_DOMAIN, and the customer-sales snapshot.
  - A genome fragment that carries no row is treated as money (fails closed).
  - Other genome records stay business-wide.
  - A staff position's turn uses the modules its position resolved.

**SEC-W1FPMS-4 (memberless proposals, D-73/D-93)**
- When the reader is null, every proposal record is replaced by memberlessProposalView. Reader null covers a contact-only bridge position, a SUPER_ADMIN who is no member and a removed member. Proposal records are GOVERNANCE_DECISION ledger rows, their bridged business_events and cognitive_events copies, and genome KEY_ACTION_PROPOSAL / GOVERNANCE_DECISION records.
- The view keeps the record's id, store and event-type title. Its content becomes, for example, 'proposal propose, status PENDING, risk LOW'.
  - Action, status and risk level are each shown only when they are one plain word.
  - They are read from the ledger row (its action column and `after`), or for a bridged copy from the ledger input it carries.
  - Title, rejection reason, approver or rejecter and figures never render.
- Members still see proposals whole, which keeps them business-wide.

**COR-W1FPMS-1 follow-up**
- Cognitive fragments carry their payload in metadata.payload. Business-event fragments carry actorType and action.
- eventPayloadOf reads the carried payload and no longer parses the rendered content. A task record without a payload fails closed.

**GREEN**
- The DoD is met. The blind STAFF member and memberless turns get no FINANCE_SNAPSHOT_COMPUTED, cross-domain or customer-sales memory, and memberless turns get no proposal title or figure. The owner, the revenue reader, the role-default STAFF member and the revenue holder's bridge position still see the money memory. Members still see proposal titles.
- The perception suites pass.
- Each of nine mutations of the fix fails the unit specs.
- Release 0 is unchanged (r0_impact KEEP): no Release 0 manifest or required case was edited.
- Cleanup is done: the database was dropped, Redis 6379 db 1 flushed, the worktree removed and pruned, and the branch kept.

built.what:
The identity business reads now give accountantEmail and the four default ledger account ids (defaultCashAccountId, defaultArAccountId, defaultApAccountId, defaultTaxAccountId) only to a reader with revenue read on that business. Revenue read is checked exactly as ModuleScopeGuard checks it for GET /finance/businesses/:id/settings: the explicit permissionScopes map (a JSON array counts as a map with nothing in it), otherwise the role defaults; SUPER_ADMIN passes. So for every member the identity reads give those columns exactly when GET settings does (V71F-C01 proves this per member kind).

Changes in IdentityService:
- New BUSINESS_FINANCE_SETTINGS_FIELDS and withholdBusinessFinanceSettings().
- getBusiness(businessId, viewer?): the GET :businessId route now passes the authenticated member (null if none, which means no access).
- listBusinesses(userId, userRole?): reads the caller's own membership of each business through a relation include, which is never sent back, and applies the rule per business.
- bootstrapUser applies the same rule to the business it returns. That business can be one the caller is only a member of (the oldest-membership case in ensureBootstrapWorkspace).

Every other column stays for every member: currency, the default tax rate (the invoice form and business settings page read it), accountingBasis, fiscalYearStartMonth, timezone, profile, masked metaData and the v1 settings.

In-process server reads with no viewer (the KEY settings adapter, the document-guidance route) still get the full row, as before. The owner-only profile PATCH (D-11) is unchanged.

Comments that called the GET settings gate "not a confinement" are updated in finance.controller.ts and books-read-scope.spec.ts (comment only). The REST scope census now records SEC-V71-2 as closed.
